about.title: Roseville Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: A defective product does not care where you bought it. Whether it was a space heater from a store off Douglas Boulevard, a power tool picked up along Pleasant Grove Boulevard, or a replacement tire installed before a drive down I-80, the question in a California product liability claim is the same: was the product defective, and did that defect hurt you? With roughly 130,000 residents in Placer County, Roseville has no shortage of homes, garages and job sites where products get put to work every day. Under California's strict liability rules, you generally do not need to prove the manufacturer was careless. You need to show a design flaw, a manufacturing error, or a missing or inadequate warning, plus a link between that defect and your injury. The manufacturer, the distributor and the retailer can each be on the hook. LawProactive is not a law firm. We are a free service that connects Roseville residents with an independent attorney who handles product cases on contingency. Keep the product, keep the packaging, and reach out when you are ready.

items.title: Strict Liability Means a Different Kind of Case
items.desc: In California you usually do not have to prove the company was negligent, only that the product was defective and that the defect caused your injury. The attorneys in our network know how to frame a claim around that standard.

items.title: Evidence Preservation From Day One
items.desc: The product itself is the heart of a defect case. An attorney can help you secure it, along with receipts, packaging and photos, before anything gets thrown away or repaired.

items.title: Every Link in the Chain Considered
items.desc: Manufacturers, distributors and retailers may all share responsibility under California law. Your attorney can look at who made, shipped and sold the product rather than stopping at the first name on the box.

items.question: A defective airbag or tire seemed to make my crash on I-80 near Roseville worse. Is that a car accident case or a product case?
items.answer: It can be both. Roseville recorded 808 injury collisions in 2025, and some crashes involve a vehicle part that did not perform as designed. An attorney can evaluate whether a design, manufacturing or warning defect played a role, which may open a separate claim against the maker or seller in addition to any claim against another driver. Do not have the vehicle repaired or scrapped until someone has looked at it.

items.question: Do I have to prove the manufacturer was careless?
items.answer: Generally, no. California product liability often runs on strict liability, so the focus is on whether the product had a defect and whether that defect caused your injury. That is a lower hurdle than proving negligence, though the facts still have to be documented carefully.

items.question: I threw away the box and I do not have the receipt. Can I still pursue a claim?
items.answer: Possibly. The most important thing is the product itself, so keep it exactly as it is, even if it is broken. Bank statements, online order histories, photos and medical records can help fill in the gaps, and an attorney can advise on what else may be useful.
